requirements.text: The interface between the CMIB, MCCC, and CPCC shall be Ethernet (IEEE 802.3 compliant) of 100 Mbits/sec or better data rate.
The interface shall be transformer coupled copper twisted pair unless other materials are required for noise (RFI), ground isolation, or physical layout constraints (long distances).
Network switches shall be employed to distribute traffic within a correlator rack and where their use will significantly reduce overall network wiring complexity.
The MCCC-CMIB, MCCC-CPCC, and MCCC-EVLA M&C networks shall be on separate physical interfaces.
There shall be a redundant communication path (serial RS-232c or equivalent) between the MCCC and CPCC to provide for remote reboot in the event of a networking or computing failure.
The interface between the MCCC and external networks (EVLA M&C) shall be Ethernet (IEEE 802.3 compliant) of 100 Mbits/sec or better data rate.
Pathways penetrating the correlator shielded room shall be fiber optic or other low RFI material to meet RFI specifications.
Network routers/switches shall be employed at the MCCC-EVLA M&C interface level (or higher) to protect the MCCC from unauthorized access and irrelevant network traffic.
The CMIB daughter board shall communicate with the correlator carrier boards via either the PCI or ISA busses.
The CMIB shall be capable of reading a 16-bit identifier from the host correlator board.
The CMIB shall be able to read back the contents of all writeable hardware control registers where meaningful.
The CMIB shall have control of hardware “warm boots” such that an external command from the MCCC to reboot the CMIB shall have an option to force a hardware warm boot.
The carrier board for the CMIB shall have an externally visible indicator (LED or other) that will provide a user with a physical indication of CMIB operational status (red = fault, green = ok).

Where applicable, all computers and peripherals shall be powered though UPS type devices with sufficient capacity for the computers to safely coordinate a system wide shutdown of the correlator hardware in the event of a prolonged power outage.
All computers within the CMCS system shall have the ability for authorized users to directly access individual systems for maintenance and monitoring through remote logins.
Each computer system in the CMCS shall have a hardware based watchdog timer configured to reboot the system in the case of a system hang.
The CMIB shall conform to both electrical and physical PC104+ standards.

The CMIB shall contain 64 Mbytes or greater of SDRAM, IDE hard disk interface, minimum of one serial and one parallel interface, PCI/ISA buses, 100BaseT network interface, capacity to boot and run a generic COTS operating system in a near real-time environment from local non-volatile storage.

The MCCC shall be a high availability type general-purpose computer capable of supporting multiple Ethernet interfaces, COTS operating systems, and support server/host services for the CMIB operating system.
The MCCC shall have all required disk and file system facilities installed locally such that the system can boot and run in a stand-alone configuration.

The CPCC shall be a high availability type general-purpose computer capable of supporting a COTS operating system and have the ability to accept a large number of external hardware status signals (power, temp, etc) either directly or through external interface hardware.
The CPCC shall have all required disk and file system facilities installed locally such that the system can boot and run in a stand-alone configuration.
The CMCS processors shall be capable of meeting all data processing deadlines and anticipated future requirements
The CMCS processors shall be capable of responding to correlator hardware inputs (interrupts) in a deterministic fashion with sufficient performance to avoid data loss, corruption or overflows.
All lower system error and debug messages shall be present at the MCCC layer.
All system error and debug messages shall be categorized in a logical fashion such that message traffic can be filtered as to content, detail, and message rate.
All messages passed between CMCS system layers shall have both UTC and wall clock time stamp information appropriate for the message type.
Software shall be provided that allows an authorized user full access to all messaging, monitor, and control traffic throughout the CMCS.
A Graphical User Interface shall be provided as an interface to the CMCS test software that allows for a convenient and configurable tool to access the CMCS remotely through the VCI.
the CMCS shall be self-monitoring.
the software part of the system shall be able to perform without total system restart due to internal failure between system maintenance windows.
the hardware part of the system shall be able to perform indefinitely without complete loss of service, except in the event of total failure of primary and backup power.
the system shall be able to continue processing of all correlator configuration/control events until the queues of parameters are exhausted and external communications are restored
the system shall be able to sit at idle and resume operations with minimal (amount TBD) delay.
all system processing and interconnect hardware shall be readily accessible for maintenance, repair, replacement and/or reconfiguration.
all systems and application source code shall be available to or on the systems that execute it.
all software application modules shall be debuggable.
all software processes shall be killable, restartable, debuggable and testable with minimal impact on normal system operations.
software tools and pre-built applications that do not have source code available shall come with a complete diagnostic package and customer support.
operating system software shall either have source code available or come with sufficient diagnostics and customer support.

I/O, communications, and processing hardware shall be easily expandable, reconfigurable, augmentable and replaceable to meet increasing data traffic and processing demands imposed by EVLA science, Correlator changes, and availability of new hardware.
All users of the system shall login using some form of unique identification.
All login attempts shall be done in a secure manner.
A system administrator shall have unrestricted access to all aspects of the system.
Each user shall have a set of system access properties that defines the user’s privileges within the system.
The administrator shall have the ability to create and add a new user to the system.
The administrator shall have the ability to remove a user from the system.
The administrator shall have the ability to edit a user’s system access properties.
The administrator shall have the ability to block all access to the system for all users or selectively by user.
the system shall continue operations, although not necessarily at full capacity, on all unaffected resources during partial shutdowns for maintenance, repair and/or upgrade.
modular design principles shall be employed to the maximum extent possible.
complete and comprehensible hardware systems specifications and configuration information shall be readily available.
software system and application code shall be well documented and written in a generally familiar language or languages (preferably not more than two).
All remote login sessions and data transmissions between system components shall be encrypted using industry-standard protocols such as SSHv2 or TLS 1.3.
All access logs and security-relevant events shall be stored in a tamper-evident, append-only format with a minimum retention period of 90 days.
Remote access to the CMCS shall require multi-factor authentication and be restricted to connections originating from authorized management subnets.
The CMCS processors shall process all incoming data streams with a maximum latency of X milliseconds and a jitter of no more than Y microseconds.
The system shall be able to resume operations from an idle state within 5 seconds of receiving a start command.
UPS devices shall provide at least 30 minutes of runtime to allow for a controlled system shutdown.
System reboots shall be completed within 60 seconds, during which time the correlator shall maintain its last known valid state.
The MCCC and CPCC shall achieve 99.99% availability with a Mean Time To Repair (MTTR) of less than 15 minutes.
Define a specific recovery time objective (e.g., 'The system shall resume operations within 30 seconds of an idle-to-active transition').
Specify the expected scaling factor (e.g., 'The system shall support a 2x increase in data throughput without hardware replacement').
Specify the required duration of power backup (e.g., 'The UPS shall provide at least 15 minutes of runtime to allow for a graceful shutdown').
